result.text: KX-9283 is the Wi-Fi module in the Ashby tumble dryer. It connects the dryer to the Halvard Home app.
KX-3107 is the voice pairing module for the Orrin heat pump.
E-2194 means the Ashby tumble dryer’s factory reset was interrupted before its saved settings could be cleared. Your previous preferences may still be active.
E-6076 means water has remained in the dishwasher’s base for more than three minutes after draining started. A blocked filter or kinked drain hose is the usual cause.
Error E-7084 means the Vale fridge freezer’s vibration sensor has detected excessive movement while the compressor is running. An uneven position or contact with nearby furniture can cause it.
The passages do not identify part KX-3673. The listed part numbers are KX-3639, KX-1006, KX-7856, KX-1639 and KX-5646.
KX-3926 is the washable metal grease filter for the Fenwick cooker hood.
The passages do not identify part KX-6507. KX-6505 is the replacement mounting backplate for the Lumen thermostat.

E-5107 means mains power was interrupted while the compressor was running. The heat pump pauses to protect the compressor during restart. When power returns, wait five minutes before restarting it from the controller.

E-6292 means the Fenwick cooker hood has detected an electrical insulation fault in its fan motor. Stop using it and switch off its power supply; have a qualified electrician assess it before deciding whether to repair or recycle it.
The passages do not mention error E-3865, so I can’t determine what it means from the information provided.
The passages do not identify part KX-3452. They list other part numbers, so check the product’s manual or contact Halvard Home support.
KX-7011 is the sealing strip fitted beneath the Corra induction hob’s glass edge during installation. It must lie flat all the way around.
The passages do not say what error E-3873 means.
KX-1639 is the charging dock supplied with the Mira robot vacuum.
E-4805 means the dishwasher’s digital warranty record is missing its purchase date, so the warranty can’t be confirmed automatically. It does not mean the warranty has expired.
Error E-6736 means the Brio kettle’s lid locking clip isn’t holding the lid securely shut. If the clip is cracked or broken, the lid needs replacing.
Error E-3293 means the Corra induction hob’s moisture sensor detected condensation beneath the control panel and stopped heating as a precaution.
KX-9495 is the heating relay module in the Lumen smart thermostat.
The passages do not identify part KX-8033.
KX-9996 is the voice connection module in an Ashby tumble dryer.

E-7160 means the Orrin heat pump’s warranty record is missing its installation date. It’s a registration issue, not a heating fault, and doesn’t automatically mean your warranty has expired. Find your installation certificate or dated installer’s invoice and contact Halvard Home support to correct the record.
Error E-4021 on a Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher means the water hasn’t drained within three minutes. A blocked drain filter is the most common cause.
The passages don’t identify part KX-5912.
KX-2446 is the drain pump fitted to the Halvard Home Keel washing machine.
E-1216 means the Fenwick cooker hood’s control board cannot detect the fan motor’s speed. The hood stops the fan to prevent it from running without speed monitoring.
E-3946 means the Corra induction hob’s lid sensor detects that the protective lid is not fully closed.
KX-5646 is the replacement cooling fan for the Corra induction hob.
KX-7896 is the Lumen thermostat’s room temperature sensor module.
The passages do not identify error E-6779. They describe E-6763, E-6076, E-9509, E-1736, and E-6067.
KX-8645 is the removable filter for a Tessa dishwasher.
The passages don’t specify what error E-8255 means. They describe Mira error E-8250, but not E-8255.
KX-3056 is the Brio kettle’s wireless pairing module, which connects the kettle to the Halvard Home app so you can link a supported voice assistant.
The passages do not mention error E-5328, so its meaning can’t be determined from the information provided.
The passages do not identify part **KX-8618**. They list **KX-1618** as the replacement drying rack for the Ashby tumble dryer.
The passages don’t identify part KX-1377. They mention KX-5646, KX-1006, KX-3056, KX-7856, and KX-3107.
The passages do not say what error E-9454 means. They describe E-9544, which indicates the temperature sensor detected overheating during Eco mode.
E-9509 means the delay-start timer has lost its saved countdown, so the dishwasher pauses instead of starting unexpectedly.
The Brio kettle supports **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi**. If your router has separate 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks, use the 2.4 GHz one.
KX-1060 is the power recovery control module for the Corra induction hob.
The passages don’t identify error E-9215. They describe other error codes, so I can’t determine what E-9215 means from this information.

Before you leave, run a wash to clear any dirty dishes. When it finishes, unload the dishwasher and let the interior cool. Clean the filter according to the user manual and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth.

For an extended absence, switch off the electricity supply and close the water supply valve. If it’s safe, leave the door slightly open so moisture can escape. If the cottage could freeze, ask a qualified installer whether the appliance should be drained. On your return, restore both supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.

Stop cooking and switch off the hob. Remove pans only when it’s safe, and let hot surfaces cool. Check that the controls are clean and dry and nothing is covering them. If it’s safe to reach the wall isolator, turn the power off for 60 seconds, then restore it.

If the error returns, leave the hob off and contact Halvard Home support. Note the exact error message and when it appears. Don’t remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

The passages give different warranty periods: one says two years from purchase (P1), while another says 66 months from delivery (P5). Check your warranty paperwork or contact Halvard Home to confirm which applies to your Fenwick cooker hood.

Frost or ice inside the dishwasher is not normal. Don’t start a programme: switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or sharp tools to remove the ice.

Leave visitors a short, clear set of instructions for the appliance:

- **Washer:** Check laundry care labels, measure detergent for the load and local water hardness, and make sure the water is on before starting. Keep the load suitable for the programme. After use, remove laundry and trapped items, wipe the door seal, switch off the machine and turn off its water supply. Leave the door slightly open, away from children and pets.
- **Dryer:** Check care labels, remove items unsuitable for tumble drying, and don’t overload the drum. Clean the lint filter after every load and keep the area around the dryer clear. Ask visitors to stay in the property while it runs and let the programme, including its cooling stage, finish. Between stays, check that the drum is empty and the filter clean; unplug the dryer if the property will be empty for an extended period.

Set a scheduled start time rather than a delay duration. For example, if you want heating to start one hour after 18:00, set the start time to 19:00, choose your target temperature, and save. Make sure the schedule is enabled and applies to the right day. Heating will start only if the room is cooler than the target temperature.

Stop the dryer immediately. Switch it off and unplug it if you can do so safely, and don’t run it again to test it. If there’s smoke or flame, keep the door closed, leave the property and call 999; don’t use water or move the appliance. If there are no signs of fire, leave it unplugged until it has cooled, then clean the lint filter and check that external vents are clear. Don’t use it again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Note the exact message or code on the display. While it’s unplugged, clean the lint filter, check any accessible air vents, and empty and securely refit the water container if your model has one. Reconnect it and try the programme once. If the message returns, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support with the code and model details. Don’t remove panels or attempt internal repairs; if you notice smoke or a burning smell, don’t restart it.
Keep the extractor running for **10 minutes after cooking** to clear lingering steam and smells.

For a Fenwick cooker hood, check that the wall switch or fused spur is on, then try the light and fan controls to see whether the hood has power. Switch it off at the electrical supply for 60 seconds, switch it back on, and try again.

If the fan and light work but the screen stays blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring; arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues.
Hire a qualified heat pump installer to disconnect, move and recommission your Orrin heat pump. Don’t move it while it’s connected to electrical wiring or pipework.

To safely move an Ashby tumble dryer:

1. Switch it off, unplug it from the wall socket, and let it cool completely if it has been running.
2. Remove the laundry, clean the lint filter and empty the water tank if fitted.
3. Disconnect any vent or drain hose, and secure the hoses and power cable so they cannot drag or catch.
4. Plan a clear route. Use two people and a suitable appliance trolley; keep the dryer upright. Never lift it by the door or control panel.
5. Protect the cabinet with blankets and secure the dryer so it cannot shift during transport.
6. At the new location, place it on a firm, level floor and reconnect it according to the installation instructions. Keep ventilation openings clear.

The safety guidance also says to leave the dryer unplugged for **38 hours after moving** before switching it on.
Yes. A factory reset of the Lumen thermostat clears saved Wi-Fi details, heating schedules, and personal settings. You’ll need to reconnect to Wi-Fi and set up your heating preferences again.

Send the service team your hob’s full model details, a clear photo of the part if you still have it, and a short description of what you need. If the part is missing, describe what it does. For a repair visit, include the fault symptoms and any display message; they may also ask for your serial number and proof of purchase.

Make sure your Mira vacuum is online in the Halvard Home app and that you can start a cleaning from the app. Then, in your voice assistant’s app, add smart home devices, search for and select **Halvard Home**, and sign in with the same Halvard Home account you used to set up Mira. Allow access and ask the assistant to discover devices.

Give the vacuum a simple name, such as “Mira,” then try saying, “Start Mira.” If it doesn’t appear, check its internet connection, unlink Halvard Home from the assistant app, and link it again.
The Brio kettle warranty lasts **47 months from the date it is delivered to you**. A separate guarantee for paid repairs lasts **122 days**.

To update your laundry appliance’s firmware, finish any active wash or drying programme, empty the drum, and leave the appliance switched on and connected to your home Wi-Fi.

- **Keel washing machine:** In the Halvard Home app, select the machine, then go to **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available.
- **Ashby tumble dryer:** On the dryer’s display, go to **Settings > Software update > Check for updates**. Select **Install** if an update is available.

Follow the on-screen instructions. Don’t switch off or unplug the appliance while it’s updating, and wait for confirmation that the update is complete before using it. If an update fails, check your Wi-Fi and try again.

To safely relocate your built-in Corra cooktop:

1. Switch it off and let the glass cool completely. Remove cookware and loose items.
2. Have a qualified electrician isolate and disconnect it if it is hardwired. Don’t cut, pull or handle the fixed wiring yourself; don’t assume a dark display means it’s isolated.
3. Have the installer release any fixings or seals. Clear the route and use two people or suitable lifting equipment, supporting the appliance’s body—not its cable, controls or exposed glass edges. Protect the glass from knocks and keep heavy objects off it.
4. Keep the cooktop from sliding or being crushed during transport, and do not tilt it more than **54 degrees**.
5. After moving it, leave it disconnected and wait **17 hours** before switching it on. Have a qualified installer check its condition, stability, ventilation, cable routing and electrical safety before use. If it was dropped, struck or exposed to water, leave it disconnected and have it checked.

Make sure the controller is powered on and responding, and connect your phone to your home Wi‑Fi with Bluetooth enabled. Stay close to the controller while searching. In your phone’s settings, allow the companion app any requested Bluetooth, nearby-device, or local-network permissions. Then fully close and reopen the app and try adding the controller again.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and check for app updates. Avoid factory-resetting the controller; contact the manufacturer’s support if the issue continues.

If you’ll leave food inside, keep the refrigerator running: set the fridge to **4°C** and the freezer to **−18°C**, make sure both doors close fully, and remove food that will expire before you return.

If you’ll empty it for the whole absence, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, wash the inside with warm water and mild detergent, and dry it thoroughly. Leave both doors ajar to help prevent smells and mould. When you return, let it reach its set temperatures before putting food back in.

In chilly weather, warm, moist cooking air can condense on the hood’s cold surfaces, forming droplets. This is more likely if the extraction duct passes through an unheated space. Run the hood while cooking and for 10 minutes afterwards, and keep the kitchen’s ventilation openings clear.

Icy or damp conditions can occur when warm, moist air gets into the fridge. Frequent door opening, uncovered food, or a door that doesn’t seal properly can contribute. Make sure the door closes fully, cover food, and clean and dry the door seal. Set the fridge to 4°C and keep the air vents clear.

Stop the programme and note the exact error code. Switch the washer off and unplug it for five minutes, then check that the door is fully closed and no clothing is caught in the seal. Don’t force the door open if water remains inside. If the error returns, stop using the washer and contact Halvard Home support, telling them the code and when it appeared.

For a Fenwick cooker hood, provide Halvard Home customer support with the **full model details from the appliance’s rating label** and the **name or a short description of the accessory** you need. If you still have it, include one clear photo; if you’re unsure what it’s called, explain what you want to replace.

Ask support to confirm it fits your exact model, is available, and to give you the total price including delivery and the expected delivery time before you order. Don’t rely on appearance alone.

To prepare your Keel washer for a move:

1. Switch it off at the socket and unplug it, using dry hands. Turn off the water supply, then disconnect the inlet and drain hoses as instructed.
2. Drain any remaining water according to the user manual, and keep a towel and shallow tray handy for spills.
3. Empty and dry the drum. Secure the hoses and cable so they cannot trail, leak or get stretched.
4. Refit the original transport bolts as directed in the manual. If they are missing or you cannot fit them safely, contact Halvard Home before moving it.
5. Keep the washer upright, use two people to move it, and do not lift it by the door, drawer, controls, hoses or cable. Plan a clear route and stop if the load becomes unstable.

At the new house, remove the transport bolts before using the washer. Follow the installation instructions, and check that it is level and the hoses are securely connected.

Switch on the Mira’s child lock by pressing and holding its power button for 3 seconds while the vacuum is on and stationary. Wait for the confirmation sound. This locks the buttons on the vacuum; scheduled cleaning and controls in the Halvard Home app remain available, so it may still start automatically. Keep your toddler away while it is moving.

Have a qualified heat pump installer disconnect the unit and safely recover its refrigerant—don’t cut pipes, open the refrigerant circuit, or dismantle it yourself. Then arrange recycling through your replacement installer or contact your local council for a service that accepts heat pumps. Check collection arrangements before moving it, keep it upright and away from children while waiting, and use a licensed waste carrier if arranging transport yourself.
Your Vale fridge freezer needs a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**.

For the Mira robot vacuum, place it on its plugged-in charging dock. Hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, then release them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave the vacuum on the dock while it restarts.

The factory reset erases saved Wi‑Fi details, maps and cleaning schedules. After it restarts, add the vacuum again in the Halvard Home app, reconnect it to Wi‑Fi, and set up your maps and schedules again.

Start with the power supply: make sure the plug is fully inserted and the wall socket is switched on. Test the socket with a working lamp. If it works, unplug the dryer for 60 seconds, reconnect it, close the door firmly and try again. Don’t use it if the plug or cable is damaged, burnt-smelling or unusually hot.

Switch off the automatic floor cleaner and remove it from its charging dock. Check the opening, hinges and catch for dust, hair or objects, and wipe accessible edges with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated properly and nothing sticks out above it, then lower the cover gently—don’t force it. If it still won’t stay down or a hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the cleaner and contact Halvard Home support.

Use heating schedules to match your routine, with lower temperatures while you’re out or asleep. For a heat pump, start around 19°C, try only a small overnight reduction, and avoid switching it off completely; this helps keep the home comfortable while using less energy. If you’re away in cold weather, keep the heat pump connected and use its holiday setting or a suitably low temperature.

For other appliances, set your fridge to 4°C and freezer to −18°C, keep their doors closed, and don’t block the vents. On an induction hob, use the lowest setting that cooks the food, turn it down to a gentle simmer after boiling, and use lids and only the water you need.

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your Keel washer’s model details and a description of the part you need. Take a clear photo of the identification label and, if you have it, the existing part. Tell support whether it’s a replacement or an extra, and ask them to confirm it fits your exact model, its availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before ordering.
First, check the cooker hood’s power supply: make sure its wall switch or fused connection switch is on. If it has a plug, check it is fully inserted only if you can reach it safely.

Check that food, bottles or packaging aren’t blocking the door, and make sure drawers and shelves are seated correctly. Clean the door seal and the surface it touches with a soft cloth and warm water, then dry them. If it’s a freezer door, check for ice buildup; don’t chip it with a sharp tool or force the door shut. If the door still hangs unevenly or the seal is split, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the kettle, then let it cool completely. Lift it off the base and dry the outside. Check whether water has run down from the spout or lid, and keep the water below the MAX mark. If water is escaping from the bottom or the puddle keeps returning, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support.

If the plug or socket is wet, don’t touch it—switch off the electricity at the consumer unit first. Don’t immerse the base or try to repair the kettle yourself.

Unplug the teapot and let it cool completely, then empty it. Use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following its package instructions for the amount, water temperature and treatment time. Don’t exceed the maximum fill mark or mix cleaning products.

After descaling, empty and rinse the teapot thoroughly. Fill it to the maximum mark, boil the water and discard it; repeat once before making drinks. Keep the base, plug and exterior dry, and never immerse the teapot in water.

First, check its power supply. If it has a clearly labelled wall switch, make sure it’s on; you can switch it off, wait 30 seconds, and turn it back on. If the display may simply be asleep, tap it once. For a battery-powered controller, try fresh batteries of the specified type, matching the + and − markings. Don’t remove the cover or touch wiring.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum and restart the programme—never force the door open.

Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, all four feet touch the floor and it does not rock when gently pushed. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transport bolts were removed. Stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support if strong vibration continues.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry—never touch a wet plug or socket. Wipe up the water, then check visible inlet-hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether water is coming from the detergent drawer. Don’t run another cycle while the cause is unclear.

If the hoses seem secure or water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support to arrange an assessment. Don’t remove panels or try to repair the leak yourself.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it into a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Dry the tank and the vacuum’s underside with a cloth. Don’t rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while it’s wet.

If the tank is cracked or it leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

For your Tessa dishwasher:

1. Make sure it’s connected to your home Wi‑Fi, switched on, empty, and not running a wash programme.
2. On the control panel, open **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**.
3. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected during installation.
4. Wait for the display to confirm the update is complete before starting a wash.

If the download fails, check your internet connection and try again. If installation keeps failing, contact Halvard Home support and describe what the display shows.
An Orrin heat pump warms your home gradually, and its radiators may feel cooler than boiler radiators. This does not necessarily indicate a fault.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try these steps in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone’s settings.
3. Turn Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Completely close and reopen the app, then try adding the heat pump again.
5. Check your app store for an update.

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Before first use:

- Read the supplied installation instructions and check that the location meets the required clearance and ventilation requirements.
- Choose a dry indoor space with a firm, level floor. Adjust the feet until the dryer stands securely without rocking, and keep ventilation openings clear of carpets, furniture and other obstructions.
- Remove all packaging from inside and around the drum.
- Connect any vent hose or water drainage required by your model according to the supplied instructions.
- Plug the dryer directly into a suitable, accessible, earthed wall socket. Do not use an extension lead or adaptor. Don’t connect it if the cable, plug or appliance appears damaged; seek qualified help if you’re unsure about the electrical supply.
- Wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth before use.

Keep the instruction booklet for guidance, and don’t use the dryer if it cannot be installed securely or safely.
Your Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi-Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.

Make sure the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network** (5 GHz won’t work for setup), turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app to access nearby devices.

Close and reopen the Halvard Home app, then try adding the machine again and follow its pairing instructions. If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and retry once Wi‑Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and provide your phone model and where setup stops.

Yes. Water under the outdoor unit during or shortly after defrosting is usually normal: ice on the coil melts and drains away. Monitor it to see whether it stops. If water runs continuously, comes from a pipe joint, or you can’t safely identify the source, contact Halvard Home support or a qualified heat pump engineer.
Yes. Gentle rumbling or hissing while the kettle heats is usually normal. A click when it switches off is expected too.
No. The Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting; you must switch it on manually when you’re ready to boil water.

Common causes include loose objects such as coins or keys, metal zips or buttons hitting the drum, an uneven load, or the dryer touching a wall or nearby furniture.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let the drum cool before checking for loose items. Redistribute bulky laundry and make sure the dryer stands firmly on a level floor without touching nearby surfaces. Don’t remove panels or reach underneath. If the noise continues—or you hear loud grinding—stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch the dryer off at the socket before unplugging it. Use a torch to check the area, not a candle.

If it’s safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry—it may be hot—and spread it out so heat can escape. Once the power supply is stable, plug the dryer back in, check the laundry and restart a suitable programme if needed.

If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave the dryer unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the machine, and let any hot water cool. Open the lower-front filter flap, place towels and a shallow tray underneath, then loosen the filter slowly to drain the water. Remove debris, rinse the filter, and refit it securely without forcing it. Run a short rinse or drain cycle to check. If it still drains slowly or leaks, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let it cool. Then clear and securely refit the fluff filter, empty and refit the water tank if your model has one, and check that no clothing is caught in the door. Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the light keeps flashing, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support, explaining which light flashes and when.

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the dishwasher.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow any nearby-device or location permissions the app requests.
3. Avoid using a guest Wi‑Fi network.
4. Fully close and reopen the app, then try adding the dishwasher again.
5. If it still isn’t found, switch the dishwasher off at the mains for 30 seconds, then turn it back on.

If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you tried.

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. Check for items blocking the door and gently clear loose debris around any visible drain hole. If the leak returns, contact Halvard Home support.

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects in the drum, an uneven load, or a machine that isn’t level. Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop and the door to unlock—don’t force it open. Spread heavy items evenly around the drum and check for coins, keys or other loose objects.

If the machine rocks when gently pressed at a corner, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting its feet. If it was recently installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transit bolts were removed. Stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support if you hear grinding or notice a burning smell or a leak.

1. Make sure the heat pump is on and not displaying a warning. Note your saved heating schedules and temperature preferences, as the reset will erase them.
2. On the controller, open **Settings** → **System** → **Factory reset**.
3. Select **Confirm** and leave the heat pump connected to power while the controller restarts.
4. When the home screen returns, check the date and time, then re-enter your preferred temperatures and heating schedule.

If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller does not restart, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the unit or change installer settings.
Recycle your old Halvard Home Corra induction hob as electrical equipment; do not put it in your household rubbish bin.

Make sure the Brio kettle isn’t heating. Press and hold the lock button for three seconds to switch the child lock on; the indicator lights up. To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds until the indicator goes out. The lock doesn’t lock the lid or make hot water safe to handle, so keep the kettle and cable out of children’s reach and supervise children.

Make sure your fridge freezer is connected to your home Wi-Fi and has a steady power supply. On the control panel, open **Settings**, select **Software update**, then choose **Check for updates**. If an update is available, follow the on-screen instructions.

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it during installation. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm the update is complete. If it fails, check your Wi-Fi connection before trying again.

Make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down; do not reset it while it is heating.

1. Place the kettle securely on its base.
2. Plug the base into a wall socket and switch the socket on.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice. This confirms the reset is complete.

You can then choose your settings again. If the light does not flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly and repeat the steps.

If the machine is damp from condensation, wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may mean there’s a leak.

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it with dry hands only if the plug and socket are dry. Let the machine and room warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a portable heater. Once it has thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or you find damaged hoses, contact Halvard Home support before using it again.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it’s stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and gently brush away deposits with a soft brush. For stubborn limescale, soak the filter in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush and rinse it thoroughly. Refit the filter securely before using the kettle.

Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base, or plug in water.

To factory-reset your Corra hob:

1. Remove all cookware and let the cooking zones cool. Make sure the control panel is clean and dry.
2. Switch the hob off with its power button, but leave the electrical supply connected.
3. Press and hold the **timer** and **minus** buttons together for five seconds.
4. Release them when you hear a beep.
5. Press the power button once to confirm the reset.

Switch the hob on again and re-enter any preferences you want to keep. If the controls don’t respond or the reset doesn’t complete, contact Halvard Home support. Don’t open the hob or remove it.

Check that the hob has power and your phone is nearby. Turn on Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and allow the app to access Bluetooth, nearby devices, and local network if prompted. Then close the app completely, wait 30 seconds, reopen it, put the hob into pairing mode using the app’s instructions, and search again.
